title: Random-subspace tests and trace smoothing for coordinate sweeps
main_claim: There is an absolute P such that Tr_reg|Q_n|^P ≤ 1+n^{-10} for every dyadic n, where Q_n is one Thorp coordinate sweep. So a bounded number of sweeps, i.e. O(d) physical shuffles, gives TV distance ≤ ½n^{-5}. The paper also gives a support lower bound of 2d−O(1) shuffles.

issues.location: Sec. 3.2 (contact counts), count of connected vertex sets
issues.description: The bound 'at most nΔ^{2(w-1)} connected vertex sets of size w' via a traversal of length 2(w−1) should read n(Δ+1)^{2(w−1)}, or n(eΔ)^{w−1}, because each traversal step also has a backtrack option. The difference is absorbed into C2 and C3.
issues.evidence: Each of the 2(w−1) steps is either a move to one of ≤Δ neighbours or a return to the parent, giving ≤(Δ+1) choices; with Δ=e^{C''√log n} this only changes constants.

sibling_notes: The cited companion (Routing-densities…, sections/05-strong-providers.tex, Cor 'Strong pointwise smoothing', which is Cor 6.2 in the compiled numbering) states exactly what Prop 2.1 uses. Its own proof was not audited here, and no family-238 sibling entry on the board covers that paper. This paper reaches the same O(d) conclusion as the sibling Thorp papers but self-contains everything else.
